topics.topic: Host rename, crash-recovery, and Linux documentation requirements for A17 store replacement
questions: Which exact observable rename and crash-recovery semantics, and which edition of Linux documentation, must a host satisfy for A17's store replacement to support the files_artifacts guarantee?

quotes:
6. A release runs on Linux and on no other host — the kernel that runs
   Registry's process is Linux's and so is the base image around it — no
   version named, and its Python is CPython 3.12 (owner, 2026-11-25). Another system, or a Linux or
   file system on which a call Registry's rules rely on — binding a listener
   exclusively and to IPv6 alone (A17), renaming a file into place (A17,
   A18) — does not act as Linux documents it, is unsupported: Registry neither
   tests for it nor defines what it does there.

Under
files_artifacts (A17, A18), renaming the store and a backup into place is
Linux's.

No guarantee
weakened: rule 6 names the host they were written for. No right,
limit, file, path or answer moved, and no outcome changed.
judgement.why: P2 already judged on these unchanged passages that A17 requires Linux-documented rename behavior but promises no additional flush or power-loss recovery semantics, while A20 expressly names no Linux version.
options: Preserve the no-link outcome without treating a particular no-follow opening primitive as part of the host support boundary.
Treat exclusive IPv6 binding and rename as the stated Linux-specific facilities defining that boundary.
consequences: Generation may choose any mechanism that preserves A18's no-link guarantee.
A host is not made unsupported merely because it lacks an unstated no-follow opening or flush primitive.

topics.topic: Whether A17’s live store operations are in files_artifacts scope and what guarantee they establish
questions: Does adding A17 make the live Registry store and A17's start-time store replacement/removal guarantees part of the files_artifacts review, despite the affected list naming the import file, backups and pointers but not the store; if so, which files_artifacts guarantee does A17 establish?

quotes: - files_artifacts: APPLICABLE; references: A07, A08, A16, A17, A18, A19, A20, A22; affected: M05, M10, import file, backups, pointers as references whose payload Registry never reads (R0-02)

Under
files_artifacts (A17, A18), renaming the store and a backup into place is
Linux's.

When the store's
   configured file does not exist and its directory does, Registry makes a new,
   empty store of the running release's version there at the start — no
   record but its audit sequence at 0 (M12) — under a
   temporary name — the store's name with a suffix the release declares —
   that it renames to the store's name only once the store is complete; at
   every start it first removes a file of that temporary name, left by an
   interrupted start, and no other file there — if it cannot, and the store
   is absent, the start fails; otherwise
   the store must open for reading and writing, pass the full integrity check
   — the store is a SQLite database, as v1's (L19), and the check passes when
   `PRAGMA integrity_check` answers `ok` and `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` finds
   nothing, the same as a backup's check (A18 rule 4) — and carry
   the store
   version of the running release, and a store of another version, or one
   that does not open, fails the start — bringing a store to a new version is
   a step of the release, not of the start.
judgement.why: A21 expressly reviews A17 under files_artifacts for the specific guarantee that a complete newly made store is renamed into place with Linux-documented behavior; it does not state that every files_artifacts concern applies to the whole live store merely because A17 is referenced.
options: Treat the whole live store as covered by every files_artifacts concern.
Treat A17 as supporting the specifically stated complete-store rename-into-place guarantee.
consequences: The second option matches the explicit reopened review; the affected list need not be expanded into broader path-ownership, non-execution, retrieval, or storage-isolation guarantees for the live store.
